name: City of Searcy

profile.address: 101, North Elm Street, Searcy, White County, Arkansas, 72143
profile.reading:
Searcy Information Technologies is listed under the City of Searcy, the municipal government of Searcy, Arkansas, at an address near 101 North Elm Street in the city's downtown core. Searcy is the county seat of White County and a city of roughly 23,000 people in the northeastern part of the state, about fifty miles northeast of Little Rock. It is also home to Harding University, a private university that is one of the city's largest employers alongside city and county government itself.

Unlike the commercial and wholesale data centers elsewhere in this registry, a municipal information technology department like this one is not built or marketed to host outside customers. City IT departments in a community this size typically run and maintain the systems that keep local government functioning day to day: utility billing and metering software for water and electric service, police and fire dispatch and records systems, geographic information system mapping for planning and public works, financial and payroll software, and the servers behind the city's public website and email. That kind of infrastructure is usually housed in a server room or data closet inside a municipal building rather than a purpose built data center, and it is sized for the city's own internal workloads rather than for colocation tenants.

No square footage, power capacity, cooling configuration, or construction date for this specific facility has been published by the City of Searcy, and the city does not appear to operate a public facing municipal broadband or colocation service under the Information Technology name. That is expected rather than unusual. Small city governments generally do not publish technical specifications for internal server infrastructure the way commercial operators do, both because the information has no marketing value to a government department and because publicizing detailed specifications of systems tied to public safety and utility operations offers little benefit and a small security downside. The listing here reflects the address and the operator of record rather than a claim about scale, and it should be read as municipal government infrastructure rather than a commercial data center serving outside tenants. Readers looking for more detail on this specific department are best served by contacting the City of Searcy directly.

reading: The City of Searcy, Arkansas operates a municipal government data center and network operations center out of its Information Technology Building at 107 North Elm Street, supporting internal city department operations rather than offering commercial or resident-facing services. The facility includes a 24-hour network operations center with remote environmental monitoring, offsite fiber-connected backup, and a natural gas or propane Generac generator for power redundancy, alongside fiber connections linking all city department buildings over Cisco networking equipment. The IT department maintains six storage arrays totaling 210 terabytes with fully automated daily backups and runs a Cisco Enterprise IP Telephony system supporting more than 150 desktop phones citywide. No evidence was found of a municipal broadband program extending city network or internet service to residents or local businesses, distinguishing this facility from municipally owned broadband utilities in some other US cities. Searcy's infrastructure appears to exist solely to support the city government's own departments and employee training programs.
